finalText:
Same-looking props aren't always the same underlying data. A few common causes:

1. The parent creates new functions or objects on every render — like `onClick={() => ...}` or `style={{...}}` — so the child gets a fresh reference each time, even though it looks identical.
2. The child isn't wrapped in `React.memo`. Without it, a child always re-renders when its parent does, no matter what props it gets.
3. The parent itself re-renders often — from state changes, context, or a hook — and that alone triggers every child under it.

Fastest fix: wrap the child in `React.memo`, and wrap any function or object props with `useCallback` or `useMemo` in the parent so they keep the same reference between renders.
